items.title: Fppf coverings and the fppf site
items.statement: Fix a base scheme $S$ ([[def-scheme]], [[def-scheme-over-base]]). An fppf covering of an $S$-scheme $T$ is a family $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ of morphisms of $S$-schemes ([[def-morphism-of-schemes]]) such that each $T_i\to T$ is flat ([[def-flat-morphism-schemes]]) and locally of finite presentation ([[def-locally-finite-presentation-morphism]]) and the images of $|T_i|\to|T|$ cover $T$. The fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ is the category of $S$-schemes with the pretopology whose coverings are the fppf coverings. A Zariski open cover is an fppf covering ([[def-open-immersion-schemes]]); fppf coverings are stable under base change and under composition: if $\{T_i\to T\}$ is fppf and $\{T_{ij}\to T_i\}$ is fppf for every $i$, then $\{T_{ij}\to T\}$ is fppf ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]). We work inside a fixed big fppf site of $S$-schemes; joint surjectivity is a topological condition and the index set need not be finite.
items.strategy: Definition with the standard stability checks, following Stacks, *Topologies on Schemes*, Section 34.7 (tags 021L, 021P, 021Q, 021R, 021S) and Vistoli, *Notes on Grothendieck topologies, fibered categories and descent theory*, Sections 2.3.1-2.3.2. Base change uses only the stability of flat and locally finitely presented morphisms; composition and refinements use Stacks Topologies Lemma 34.4.2. No choice principle enters the definition. The big-site conventions are those of [[def-scheme-over-base]]; nothing below depends on size questions beyond those conventions.

items.title: Groupoids in schemes, relations and etale equivalence relations
items.statement: A groupoid in $S$-schemes is a tuple $(U,R,s,t,c,e,i)$ of $S$-schemes and morphisms $s,t\colon R\to U$ (source and target), $c\colon R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ (composition), $e\colon U\to R$ (identity) and $i\colon R\to R$ (inverse) satisfying the usual identities of a small groupoid ([[def-morphism-of-schemes]], [[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]], [[def-scheme-over-base]]). With $j=(t,s)\colon R\to U\times_SU$, the groupoid is a relation when $j$ is a monomorphism ([[def-monomorphism-and-epimorphism]]); then $j$ presents $R$ as a reflexive, symmetric and transitive set-theoretic relation on $U$. An equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$ is a groupoid in $S$-schemes that is a relation. It is an etale equivalence relation when in addition $s$ and $t$ are etale ([[def-etale-morphism-schemes]]). For a morphism of $S$-schemes $g\colon U'\to U$ the restriction $R'=R|_{U'}$ is the base change $R\times_{U\times_SU}(U'\times_SU')$ with source and target the two projections, equipped with the base-changed groupoid structure; restricting an equivalence relation gives an equivalence relation ([[def-equivalence-relation]] gives the underlying set-theoretic notion).
items.strategy: Definition and well-definedness checks following Stacks, *Groupoids*, Definition 39.3.1, Lemma 39.3.2 and Definition 39.9.1 (tags 022P, 022Q), and Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Definition 65.9.2 (tag 02WS) for the etale case. A monomorphism $j\colon R\to U\times_SU$ encodes a subfunctor of $U\times_SU$, and the maps $s,t,c,e,i$ encode the relation operations and their axioms; the groupoid axioms are the usual commutativity of the standard diagrams. Vistoli Sections 3.4 and 3.5 give the same structure in fibred-category language. Etale morphisms are stable under base change (published [[lem-etale-stable-base-change-composition]]), so restrictions along etale morphisms of etale equivalence relations are etale equivalence relations; this is recorded separately as [[lem-etale-equivalence-relation-restriction]].

items.title: Categories fibred in groupoids over a site
items.statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category ([[def-category]]). A functor $p:\mathcal S\to\mathcal C$ is a category fibred in groupoids if every arrow $f:V\to U$ and object $x$ over $U$ admits a cartesian arrow $\varphi:y\to x$ over $f$, and each fibre category $\mathcal S_U$ is a groupoid ([[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]], [[def-isomorphism-groupoid-and-connected-category]]). Here cartesian means: for any $g:W\to V$, object $z$ over $W$ and arrow $\psi:z\to x$ with $p(\psi)=fg$, there is a unique $\chi:z\to y$ over $g$ with $\varphi\chi=\psi$. The fibre $\mathcal S_U$ has objects over $U$ and morphisms over $\mathrm{id}_U$. Equivalently every arrow of $\mathcal S$ is cartesian and lifts exist for every $f,x$. A 1-morphism is a functor over $\mathcal C$ (which automatically preserves cartesian arrows); a 2-morphism is a natural transformation over $\mathcal C$ ([[def-natural-transformation]]). Such a 1-morphism is an equivalence precisely when it induces fully faithful essentially surjective functors on all fibres. These objects, functors and natural transformations form a strict 2-category: functor composition is strictly associative. Chosen pullback functors instead compose up to the canonical isomorphisms supplied by cartesian uniqueness; choosing a global cleavage may use AC and is not required by the definition.
items.strategy: Use Vistoli3.5 and3.21, with the full3.22 argument. If all arrows are cartesian and lifts exist, the category is fibred. Applying the universal property to an arrow over an identity gives a right inverse; that inverse also has a right inverse, so every vertical arrow is an isomorphism. Conversely, in a fibred category with groupoid fibres, any arrow $y\to x$ factors through a cartesian lift $y'\to x$ by a unique vertical arrow $y\to y'$, which is an isomorphism; hence the original arrow is cartesian. Thus every base-preserving functor preserves cartesian arrows (Vistoli3.23). Full faithfulness on fibres plus cartesian factorization gives full faithfulness on each hom-set over a fixed base arrow; essential surjectivity fibrewise gives equivalence over the base. The definition requires neither a cleavage nor a simultaneous choice of pullbacks. Pseudofunctors arise only after choosing pullbacks, while the concrete functor 2-category has strict composition.

items.title: Simplicial objects, simplicial commutative rings and homotopy groups
items.statement: Let $\Delta$ be the simplex category, with objects the finite nonempty ordered sets $[n]=\{0<\dots<n\}$ and morphisms the order-preserving maps. A simplicial object in a category $\mathcal C$ is a functor $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ ([[def-category]], [[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]]); a simplicial set is a simplicial object in sets, a simplicial commutative ring is a simplicial object in commutative rings ([[def-commutative-ring]]), and a simplicial module over a simplicial ring is a simplicial object in modules with compatible action. Face and degeneracy maps are the images of the maps $[n-1]\to[n]$ that omit, respectively repeat, an index; they satisfy the usual simplicial identities. The Moore complex of a simplicial abelian group or module $M_\bullet$ is the chain complex with $M_n$ in degree $n$ and differential $d_n=\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^id_i$ ([[def-chain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]]); its homology is written $\pi_n(M_\bullet)=H_n(M_\bullet)$ ([[def-homology-object-of-a-chain-complex]]). For a simplicial commutative ring $A_\bullet$ this defines $\pi_n(A_\bullet)$ for $n\ge0$, with $\pi_0(A_\bullet)$ a commutative ring and each $\pi_n(A_\bullet)$ a $\pi_0(A_\bullet)$-module. A morphism of simplicial rings is a weak equivalence when it induces isomorphisms on all $\pi_n$; the category of derived rings is the localization of simplicial commutative rings at weak equivalences ([[def-natural-transformation]]).
items.strategy: Definitions with standard conventions, following Stacks, *Simplicial Methods*, Chapter 14 (simplex category 14.2, simplicial objects 14.3, homotopy groups 14.11-14.15, Dold-Kan 14.23-14.26) and Toen, *Derived algebraic geometry*, Sections 2.1-2.2. The identification of homotopy groups with homology of the Moore complex is the Dold-Kan normalization theorem; the local convention is to define $\pi_n$ by the Moore complex, which agrees with the classical definition (Dold-Kan; Stacks Section 14.24, Theorem 14.24.3, tag 019G). The ring and module structures on $\pi_*$ are immediate from the simplicial identities. No model-category machinery is introduced in the definition; weak equivalences are used only to state that later constructions are independent of choices up to canonical isomorphism.

items.title: Bounded polynomial-factorization categories and the cotangent module diagram
items.statement: Assume AC for the size bounds and transported polynomial presentations ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a map A->B of commutative unital rings and an infinite cardinal kappa at least the sizes of A,B and of the variable sets in the specified countable polynomial resolutions. The small category $C_{B/A}^{\kappa}$ is opposite to the category whose objects are polynomial presentations $A[E]\to B$ with |E|<=kappa (using ordinal representatives and transported specified presentations) and whose arrows are A-algebra maps commuting with augmentation ([[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]], [[def-category]]). Its cotangent diagram is the contravariant functor to B-modules $F_{B/A}(P\to B)=\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB$ ([[def-kahler-differentials-algebra]], [[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]]). A simplicial polynomial resolution yields a cosimplicial object of this opposite category. A commutative ring square with A',B' gives the functor $P\mapsto P\otimes_AA'$ to the corresponding bounded category over A'->B', after taking a common bound.
items.strategy: Use the actual polynomial-factorization category of Stacks92.4, with a small bounded presentation model. There is a set of objects: ordinals lambda<=kappa, polynomial rings on lambda, and all functions lambda->B specifying their augmentations. Each hom collection is a set of assignments of the source variables to target polynomials satisfying the augmentation condition. Enlarge by the specified countable presentations or transport them degreewise to these models; conjugating all face/degeneracy maps by those algebra isomorphisms preserves the simplicial identities. A suitable infinite kappa exists under AC by bounding the countable union of the given variable sets and A,B. Since a polynomial ring on <=kappa variables over a ring of size <=kappa has size <=kappa, the standard resolution also fits at every stage. This introduces no universe axiom. Differential functoriality gives the stated contravariant module diagram and polynomial differential modules are free. Tensoring a polynomial presentation changes its coefficient ring and preserves the same variable set. Independence of further bound enlargement follows from the coefficient/category-change lemma below when a common standard resolution computes both bounded categories; no unbounded category colimit is being assumed.

items.title: Module diagrams have projective representables and computable derived colimits
items.statement: Assume AC. For a small category C and commutative ring R, the category $\mathcal A_R(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(C^{op},R\text{-Mod})$ is abelian with pointwise exactness. The diagrams $R_U=R[\operatorname{Hom}_C(-,U)]$ are projective and every diagram has a canonical epimorphism from a direct sum of them. Bounded-above projective replacements can therefore be supplied in this category, and $L\operatorname{colim}_{C^{op}}$ exists there using the published supplied-replacement derived-functor interfaces. Moreover $\operatorname{colim}R_U=R$, and for a diagram F in degree zero its derived colimit is computed by the bar complex $K_n(F)=\bigoplus_{U_n\to...\to U_0}F(U_0)$ with alternating face differential (last face uses restriction of coefficients).
items.strategy: Proof. Kernels, cokernels, finite sums and images are computed objectwise; their structure maps are induced by those of the diagrams, proving all abelian axioms and pointwise exactness. Sending a natural map R_U->F to the image of [id_U] gives Hom(R_U,F)=F(U), with inverse [a:V->U]->F(a)(s). Evaluation is exact, so R_U is projective. A direct sum of these objects is projective under AC by choosing lifts of all component maps. The epimorphism $\bigoplus_{U,s\in F(U)}R_U\to F$ sends the basis a to F(a)(s); at V, its summand (V,s) and id_V lift every s, proving epimorphy. Repeating this construction on successive kernels supplies projective resolutions. For bounded-above complexes, apply [[lem-bounded-above-complexes-admit-projective-replacements]] with these specified representable-sum epimorphisms; AC supplies its DC/lifting assumptions. The hypotheses of [[thm-projective-complexes-model-the-bounded-above-derived-category]] and [[thm-existence-of-the-bounded-above-left-total-derived-functor]] are thereby instantiated, rather than assumed for the diagram category. Apply colimit to the supplied projective models. Each generator [a:V->U] in R_U identifies in its colimit with [id_U], while the augmentation sending every [a] to 1 shows this generator has no extra relation; hence colim R_U=R. Finally K is an exact functor from diagrams to chain complexes, since each degree is a direct sum of evaluations. For R_U its basis is a chain U_n->...->U_0 together with a map U_0->U. Appending that final map and U gives an extra degeneracy; with sign (-1)^{n+1} it contracts the augmented complex onto R. Thus K(P) has no higher homology for every projective representable sum P. For a projective resolution G_p->F, the first-quadrant double complex K_q(G_p) augments in one direction to K(F), with exact rows by pointwise exactness, and in the other to colim G, with exact columns by the contraction. Finite-diagonal totalization therefore makes both maps quasi-isomorphisms: kill a cycle's component of largest positive row/column index by an augmented exactness lift and descend the index until it is zero. This proves K(F) computes the derived colimit canonically and functorially. The bar description also gives the canonical change-of-category map by applying a functor to each chain. The representable-sum epimorphism at every replacement stage is defined from all elements of the required diagram; this supplies a uniform objectwise replacement assignment and does not assume a choice function on a proper class. Homotopy-class comparison arrows between its models are supplied by projective lifting under AC and uniquely determined in the localized category.

items.title: Fppf sheaves of sets and sheafification
items.statement: A presheaf of sets on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ ([[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]]) is a contravariant functor to the category of sets ([[def-presheaf-representable-functor-and-representation]], [[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]]). It is an fppf sheaf when for every fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ the diagram $F(T)\to\prod_iF(T_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}F(T_i\times_TT_j)$ is an equalizer in sets ([[def-equivalence-relation]], [[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]); equivalently, restriction identifies $F(T)$ with the set of families $(s_i)$ whose two pullbacks to each $T_i\times_TT_j$ agree. A morphism of presheaves is a natural transformation ([[def-natural-transformation]]). The sheafification of a presheaf $F$ is an fppf sheaf $F^{\mathrm a}$ with a morphism $F\to F^{\mathrm a}$ such that every morphism $F\to G$ with $G$ an fppf sheaf factors uniquely through $F\to F^{\mathrm a}$; it is unique up to unique isomorphism when it exists. Representable presheaves are fppf sheaves ([[lem-nonaffine-fppf-descent-of-scheme-morphisms]]), under the Axiom of Choice recorded there. All sheaves below are set-valued unless stated otherwise.
items.strategy: Definitions and conventions; existence of the sheafification is proved separately as [[lem-fppf-sheafification-exists]]. The equalizer form of the sheaf condition is Stacks, *Sites and Sheaves*, Section 7.7 (tag 00VM) and Vistoli Section 2.3.3. That representable functors are fppf sheaves is the published [[lem-nonaffine-fppf-descent-of-scheme-morphisms]], which assumes AC. Sheafification preserves finite limits, used below only for fibre products and monomorphisms of sheaves; this follows from the explicit plus construction in [[lem-fppf-sheafification-exists]].

items.title: Restriction of an etale equivalence relation
items.statement: Let $j\colon R\to U\times_SU$ be an etale equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$ ([[def-groupoid-in-schemes-and-etale-equivalence-relation]]) and let $g\colon U'\to U$ be a morphism of $S$-schemes. Form the restriction $R'=R|_{U'}=R\times_{U\times_SU}(U'\times_SU')$ with source and target the standard projections ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]). Then $j'\colon R'\to U'\times_SU'$ is an equivalence relation on $U'$ over $S$; if $g$ is etale, then $j'$ is an etale equivalence relation. When $g$ is etale, each restricted source/target is a composition of a base change of $g$ and a base change of $s$ or $t$, hence etale.
items.strategy: Use the actual restriction $R'=U'\times_{g,U,s}R\times_{t,U,g}U'$. Its points are triples $(u'_1,r,u'_2)$ with $s(r)=g(u'_1)$ and $t(r)=g(u'_2)$. Its map to $U'\times_SU'$ is a base change of the relation monomorphism. Identities, inverses and compositions restrict on both endpoints by the groupoid formulas, so it is an equivalence relation for any $g$. If $g$ is etale, the projection to either $U'$ factors through a base change of $g$ followed by a base change of $s$ or $t$; both factors are etale by [[lem-etale-stable-base-change-composition]]. This is exactly Stacks02WT and Groupoids3.3/18.1; restricting only one endpoint does not define a relation on $U'$.

items.title: Descent data for schemes over an fppf covering
items.statement: Let $\{X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be an fppf covering of an $S$-scheme $X$ ([[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]]) and put $X_{ij}=X_i\times_XX_j$, $X_{ijk}=X_i\times_XX_j\times_XX_k$ ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]). A descent datum for schemes relative to this covering is a family of $X_i$-schemes $V_i\to X_i$ together with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}\colon \mathrm{pr}_{X_i}^*V_i\to\mathrm{pr}_{X_i}^*V_j$ over $X_{ij}$ satisfying the cocycle condition $\varphi_{ik}=\varphi_{jk}\circ\varphi_{ij}$ over $X_{ijk}$ ([[def-morphism-of-schemes]]). A morphism of descent data is a family of compatible $X_i$-morphisms. The datum is effective when there is an $X$-scheme $V$ with compatible isomorphisms $V\times_XX_i\cong V_i$ over $X_i$ for all $i$; effectiveness means precisely that the datum is in the essential image of the base-change functor.
items.strategy: Definition of Stacks, *Descent*, Definition 35.34.1 (tag 023U), specialized to the fppf coverings of [[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]]; the same notion is Vistoli Section 4.1.2. The cocycle condition is the standard one; a refinement of the covering induces an equivalence of categories of descent data (Vistoli Section 4.1.4), although this functoriality is not used below. No effectiveness is asserted in the definition.

items.title: The standard simplicial resolution of a ring map
items.statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative unital rings ([[def-ring-homomorphism]]) and for a set $S$ let $A[S]$ denote the polynomial $A$-algebra on $S$ ([[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]). The standard resolution of $B$ over $A$ is the augmented simplicial $A$-algebra $\epsilon\colon P_\bullet\to B$ with $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, and in general $P_n=A[P_{n-1}]$; the face and degeneracy maps are induced by the counit $A[\;]\to\mathrm{id}$ and unit $\mathrm{id}\to A[\;]$ of the free-forgetful adjunction, and the augmentation $\epsilon$ is induced by the structure map $A[B]\to B$ ([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]). Each $P_n$ is a polynomial $A$-algebra, and the augmentation is a weak equivalence of simplicial rings.
items.strategy: The free-forgetful comonad unit and counit define the faces, degeneracies and augmentation, and their triangle identities give the simplicial identities. The augmentation's admissibility is now proved locally by [[lem-standard-polynomial-resolution-admissibility]], which supplies the explicit underlying extra-degeneracy contraction and the normalized abelian trivial-Kan criterion. This lemma is a justified_by supplier, since it depends on this definition. No unspecified model-category theorem is imported for this ordinary standard resolution.

items.title: Simplicial sets, homotopies and trivial Kan fibrations
items.statement: A simplicial set is a contravariant functor from the simplex category $\Delta$ to sets ([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]], [[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]]). Put $\Delta[n]_k=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([k],[n])$. Its boundary $\partial\Delta[n]$ consists of the non-surjective maps $[k]\to[n]$; $\partial\Delta[0]$ is empty. Products and pullbacks of simplicial sets are computed degreewise. A simplicial homotopy from $f$ to $g$ is a map $H:X\times\Delta[1]\to Y$ restricting to $f,g$ at the two vertices. A simplicial set is contractible here when it is homotopy equivalent in this sense to the one-point constant simplicial set. A map $p:X\to Y$ is a trivial Kan fibration when every square with left side $\partial\Delta[n]\hookrightarrow\Delta[n]$, $n\ge0$, admits a diagonal lift; in degree zero this means $p_0$ is surjective. Thus this term specifies boundary lifting, not merely a quasi-isomorphism of complexes.
items.strategy: These are the exact Stacks definitions: representable simplices and their boundaries, simplicial-set homotopy, and Definition14.30.1. Face and degeneracy maps are obtained from the elementary order maps in the existing simplicial-object definition. The equality of the boundary with non-surjective maps follows by factorizing a non-surjective order map through a proper face; a surjective map contains the distinguished nondegenerate n-simplex and is outside the boundary. No AC is required for these definitions.

items.title: Sheafification exists for the fppf site
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every presheaf of sets $F$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ ([[def-fppf-sheaf-and-sheafification]]) there is an fppf sheaf $F^{\mathrm a}$ and a morphism $F\to F^{\mathrm a}$ satisfying the universal property of the sheafification; it is unique up to unique isomorphism, the unit is an isomorphism if $F$ is already a sheaf, and sheafification is functorial and commutes with finite limits of sheaves. It is computed by the two-step plus construction $F^{\mathrm a}=F^{++}$ over the fppf pretopology ([[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]]).
items.strategy: Use the full two-plus argument of Stacks Sites and Sheaves7.10 (00WB,00WG,00WH), also Vistoli2.3.7. Define F+(T) as the filtered colimit of compatible families over covers and refinements. Every plus section is locally an old F-section. Equality is equality after common refinement. These descriptions prove F+ is separated; if F is separated they show compatible plus sections glue, hence F+ is a sheaf. Therefore F++ is always a sheaf. A map F to a sheaf G sends a compatible family to its unique glued G-section, giving the unique map F++ to G and its universal property. Filtered colimits of sets commute with finite limits, and common refinements of finitely many covers exist, so the plus construction and hence sheafification preserve finite limits. The unit is an isomorphism for a sheaf. The assertion that F to F+ is universal for all separated presheaves is not used (it is false). AC is used to select cover representatives and common refinements, on the fixed big site of [[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]].

items.title: Representable morphisms of presheaves and fibrewise properties
items.statement: Let $F$ and $G$ be presheaves of sets on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ ([[def-fppf-sheaf-and-sheafification]]) and let $a\colon F\to G$ be a morphism of presheaves ([[def-natural-transformation]]). For a morphism $\xi\colon T\to G$ from an $S$-scheme $T$ the fibre product $F\times_{G,\xi}T$ is the presheaf $T'\mapsto\{(x,\varphi):x\in F(T'),\ \varphi\colon T'\to T,\ a(x)=\xi\circ\varphi\}$ ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]). We say $a$ is representable by schemes when for all $T,\xi$ this fibre product is representable by a scheme ([[def-presheaf-representable-functor-and-representation]], [[def-morphism-of-schemes]]). If $\mathcal P$ is a property of morphisms of schemes stable under base change, a representable morphism $a$ has property $\mathcal P$ when every base change to a scheme has $\mathcal P$; this defines representable etale, flat, surjective, open-immersion and closed-immersion morphisms ([[def-etale-morphism-schemes]], [[def-flat-morphism-schemes]], [[def-open-immersion-schemes]], [[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]). A representable morphism of sheaves is surjective when every section of $G$ lifts fppf-locally to $F$; an etale cover is a representable, etale, surjective morphism.
items.strategy: Definition following Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Definition 65.3.1 and Definition 65.5.1 (tags 02W9, 025V), with the fibrewise convention of Stacks 65.5.2-65.5.4 and Vistoli Chapter 2. Representability and the property calculus are fibrewise: base change of a representable morphism along any morphism of presheaves is representable, and properties stable under base change pull back; composition is handled by the corresponding scheme lemmas. Surjectivity of a morphism of sheaves is the fppf-local lifting condition, which is equivalent to surjectivity of the induced morphism of sheaves (Stacks 65.5.5). No representability is asserted for arbitrary presheaf morphisms.

items.title: Effective fppf descent for separated locally quasi-finite morphisms
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the Zariski Main and descent suppliers. Let $S$ be a scheme and let $\{X_i\to X\}$ be an fppf covering of an $S$-scheme $X$ ([[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]]). If $(V_i/X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ is a descent datum for schemes ([[def-descent-data-for-schemes]]) and each $V_i\to X_i$ is separated ([[def-separated-morphism-schemes]]) and locally quasi-finite ([[def-quasi-finite-morphism-schemes]]), then the descent datum is effective: there is a scheme $V\to X$, separated and locally quasi-finite over $X$, with compatible isomorphisms $V\times_XX_i\cong V_i$.
items.strategy: Full Stacks02W8 proof, with its prerequisites reproduced using published suppliers rather than the earlier unsupported closed-graph gluing description. Reduce over affine target opens to a single flat surjective finitely presented affine cover $X=\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$: finite affine refinements exist by openness and target quasi-compactness, and effectiveness glues by uniqueness of morphism descent. For every affine open $W^1\subseteq V$, let $W$ be its saturation under the descent transport. Because $X/R$ is flat finitely presented, saturation is open; it is quasi-compact as the image of $W^1\times_RX$, and is stable by the cocycle condition. Thus $W\to X$ is separated quasi-finite (it has finite type since $W$ is quasi-compact and locally quasi-finite). By [[lem-scheme-zariski-main-factorization-quasi-finite]] over affine $X$, it is open in a finite affine $X$-scheme, hence quasi-affine. To descend this stable quasi-affine $W$, use its canonical affinization $Z=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$. A finite affine cover of the separated $W$ has affine pairwise intersections; its equalizer description of global sections shows flat base change commutes with $\Gamma(W,-)$. It also shows that for a finite basic-open cover of $W$ inside an affine ambient scheme, localizing $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ at each defining function gives the coordinate ring of that basic open: finite denominators in the equalizer can be cleared. Hence $W\to Z$ is a quasi-compact open immersion. The descent transport induces compatible algebra descent on $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$, effective by [[lem-faithfully-flat-effective-descent-of-modules-and-algebras]], giving an affine scheme $Z_0$ downstairs. The open $W\subseteq (Z_0)_X$ is saturated, so its image $W_0$ is open under the flat finitely presented projection and its inverse image is exactly $W$; equality follows from the cocycle and the nonzero tensor product of residue fields over a common field. Thus $W_0$ descends $W$. The stable saturated opens cover $V$. Their intersections inherit the same descent, and the unique compatible open inclusions and transition isomorphisms descend by [[lem-nonaffine-fppf-descent-of-scheme-morphisms]], then glue the $W_0$ into a scheme descending $V$. This is the exact saturation/quasi-affine/effective-descent/gluing route of02W8, valid without Noetherian hypotheses. Separatedness and local quasi-finiteness descend by their affine diagonal and finite-type finite-fiber criteria on the cover. AC is inherited from Zariski Main, affine refinements and morphism descent.

items.title: Descent data, prestacks and stacks in groupoids over the fppf site
items.statement: Let $p\colon\mathcal S\to(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ be a category fibred in groupoids ([[def-category-fibred-in-groupoids]]) over the fppf site ([[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]]). For an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ write $T_{ij}=T_i\times_TT_j$ and $T_{ijk}=T_i\times_TT_j\times_TT_k$. Descent data for a family of objects $x_i$ of $\mathcal S_{T_i}$ is a family of isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}\colon x_i|_{T_{ij}}\to x_j|_{T_{ij}}$ in $\mathcal S_{T_{ij}}$ satisfying the cocycle condition $\varphi_{ik}=\varphi_{jk}\circ\varphi_{ij}$ over $T_{ijk}$; with the evident morphisms these form a category $\mathrm{DD}(\{T_i\to T\},(x_i))$. The fibred category $\mathcal S$ is a prestack when for all objects $x,y$ of $\mathcal S_T$ the presheaf $U\mapsto\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal S_U}(x|_U,y|_U)$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{fppf}$ is an fppf sheaf ([[def-fppf-sheaf-and-sheafification]]). It is a stack in groupoids when it is a prestack and every descent datum of objects is effective: for every covering the base-change functor $\mathcal S_T\to\mathrm{DD}(\{T_i\to T\})$ is an equivalence of categories. A presheaf of sets $F$ whose values are fppf sheaves determines a stack in setoids $\mathcal S_F$, with $\mathcal S_F(T)$ the discrete groupoid on $F(T)$; in particular every $S$-scheme $X$ determines the stack in groupoids $\mathcal S_X$ with fibre category over $T$ the discrete groupoid on $\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,X)$ ([[def-presheaf-representable-functor-and-representation]]).
items.strategy: Definition following Stacks, *Stacks*, Definitions 8.4.1 and 8.5.1 with Lemmas 8.4.6 and 8.5.2-8.5.6 (tags 0268, 02ZH, 02ZC, 02ZI), and Vistoli, Chapter 4, Definition 4.6 and Proposition 4.16. The equivalence between effectivity of descent data and the sieve-theoretic sheaf condition is Stacks Lemma 8.4.6; the Hom-presheaf formulation is the prestack condition. The example of a representable fibre category as a stack in setoids is Vistoli Section 3.4 and Example 3.47; it is used below to compare schemes with stacks. Conventions: 'stack' always means stack in groupoids over the fppf site; all fibre categories are groupoids by definition.

items.title: The cotangent complex of a ring map
items.statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative unital rings and let $\epsilon\colon P_\bullet\to B$ be its standard resolution ([[def-standard-resolution-of-a-ring-map]]). The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}$ is the complex of $B$-modules associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet,\epsilon}B$ ([[def-kahler-differentials-algebra]], [[def-derivation-algebra]]): in degree $n$ it is $\Omega_{P_n/A}\otimes_{P_n}B$, and the differential is the alternating sum of the face maps ([[def-shift-of-a-chain-complex]], [[def-chain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]]). It is well defined as a complex, without any choice: the standard resolution is explicitly constructed. A simplicial resolution of $B$ over $A$ is any augmented simplicial $A$-algebra $Q_\bullet\to B$ with each $Q_n$ a polynomial $A$-algebra and the augmentation a weak equivalence; the independence of $L_{B/A}$ from the chosen resolution is the comparison theorem proved below.
items.strategy: Definition 92.3.2 of Stacks, *The Cotangent Complex* (tag 08PN), following Illusie; the simplicial module is converted to a complex by the Moore-complex convention of [[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]. Because the definition uses the explicitly constructed standard resolution, its well-definedness is immediate and does not require any comparison theorem. The basic computations $H^0(L_{B/A})\cong\Omega_{B/A}$ and $L_{B/A}\simeq\Omega_{B/A}[0]$ for polynomial $B$ are recorded as [[lem-cotangent-complex-h0-and-polynomial-case]]; general resolution independence is the separate comparison statement below.

items.title: Trivial simplicial fibrations lift monomorphisms and have contractible products of fibres
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). A trivial Kan fibration of simplicial sets ([[def-simplicial-set-homotopy-and-trivial-kan-fibration]]) lifts every degreewise injective map. It is stable under pullback and set-indexed products. Every fibre over a vertex of a constant target is nonempty and contractible, and every set-indexed product of such fibres is nonempty and contractible. In particular, a trivial Kan fibration is a simplicial homotopy equivalence.
items.strategy: Proof. Every simplex has a unique nondegenerate ancestor: if $x=\alpha^*y=\beta^*z$ with alpha,beta surjective and y,z nondegenerate, take an order-preserving section xi of beta. Nondegeneracy forces alpha xi surjective, so dim(z)>=dim(y); reversing the roles gives equality. Thus alpha xi is the identity for every section xi of beta, forcing alpha=beta and y=z. Existence follows by removing degeneracies until dimension decreases to a nondegenerate simplex. Consequently adjoining a missing simplex of smallest dimension together with its degeneracies is precisely the pushout of a simplex along its boundary. For a lifting problem Z subset W, well-order the missing nondegenerate simplices by dimension and then within each dimension, using AC, and successively choose a boundary lift. At limit stages take the union. Unique nondegenerate ancestors ensure no conflicting degeneracy assignments. This proves lifting against every monomorphism. Pullback stability is the fibre-product universal property. For products solve the boundary problem coordinatewise and use AC to choose the set-indexed family of lifts. The empty product is the point. Lifting the empty subobject into Y produces a section q:Y->X. Lift $X\times\partial\Delta[1]\subseteq X\times\Delta[1]$ over Y with endpoint maps id_X and qp; the resulting H gives a homotopy from id_X to qp, while pq=id_Y. Thus p is a homotopy equivalence. A fibre is the pullback of p along a point, hence a trivial fibration over a point, and its products are likewise trivial fibrations over a point. This proves the contraction assertion. AC is used exactly in the well-order/transfinite lift selections and arbitrary product lift selection; no model-category theorem is invoked.

items.title: Normalized simplicial chains, prism homotopies and the abelian trivial-fibration criterion
items.statement: For a simplicial abelian group M, put $s(M)_n=M_n$, $d=\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^id_i$, with differential zero out of degree zero; put $N(M)_n=\bigcap_{i<n}\ker d_i$ and differential $(-1)^nd_n$ ([[def-chain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], [[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]). Inclusion $N(M)\to s(M)$ is a natural chain homotopy equivalence. A simplicial-set homotopy induces a chain homotopy on free abelian or free R-module chains. If a homomorphism of simplicial abelian groups is a homotopy equivalence of underlying simplicial sets, its associated chain map is a quasi-isomorphism. A termwise surjective homomorphism inducing a quasi-isomorphism of associated complexes is a trivial Kan fibration ([[def-simplicial-set-homotopy-and-trivial-kan-fibration]]).
items.strategy: Proof. Define $p_{n,0}=1$, $p_{n,i}=(1-s_{i-1}d_{i-1})\cdots(1-s_0d_0)$ for 1<=i<=n, and $p_n=p_{n,n}$. Applying the factors successively kills d_0,...,d_{n-1}; the earlier killed faces remain zero by the simplicial identities. Thus p_n maps to N(M)_n and is the identity there. The same identities give a chain projection p and, for $H_n=\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i s_i p_{n,i}$, the identity $dH+Hd=1-\iota p$. To verify it, expand each differential into its faces; the pairs at positions i and i+1 cancel using d_i s_i=d_{i+1}s_i=1, the faces before i commute to the earlier projection factors, and the faces after i commute past s_i. The surviving sum telescopes to $1-p_{n,n}$. This proves normalization and also its functoriality; hence N is exact, since its natural direct-summand projection commutes with every simplicial homomorphism and gives lifts for any degreewise epimorphism. For a homotopy of simplicial sets, the prism maps $h_i(x)=H_{n+1}(s_i x,(0,...,0,1,...,1))$, with i+1 zeros, give $\sum_i(-1)^ih_i$ on free chains. Expanding its boundary, the internal faces cancel in adjacent prism terms and the endpoint faces give g-f. Thus free chains preserve homotopy equivalences. To pass from underlying-set homotopy equivalence f:M->M' to group homology, compare the free abelian simplicial groups Z[M] and Z[M'] with their evaluation maps to M,M'. Every normalized cycle x lifts to the normalized free cycle [x]-[0]. If f(x) bounds, a normalized bounding y in M' lifts to [y]-[0] whose boundary, up to the displayed normalization sign, is [f(x)]-[0]. The free map is a homology isomorphism by the prism argument. Lifting a free cycle proves surjectivity on group homology; a lifted cycle mapping to this free boundary proves injectivity. For the final lifting criterion, let f:M->M' be termwise epic with acyclic kernel K. A boundary-lifting problem in degree n first lifts its target simplex and subtracts that lift from the prescribed faces, reducing to K->0. In degree zero choose a lift directly. For n>=1 fill the first n faces inductively: begin u=s_0x_0 and replace u by $u+s_r(x_r-d_ru)$ for r=1,...,n-1. The identities and face compatibility preserve the previously filled faces. The remaining discrepancy z=x_n-d_nu has every face zero, hence is a normalized cycle in K_{n-1}. Normalization and acyclicity give w in N(K)_n with $(-1)^nd_nw=z$. Then u+(-1)^nw fills the last face while leaving the others fixed. This supplies every boundary lift, proving the exact trivial-Kan criterion without an ambient model category.

items.title: The fppf quotient sheaf of a pre-relation
items.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and let $s,t\colon R\to U$ be morphisms of $S$-schemes ([[def-morphism-of-schemes]]). For an $S$-scheme $T$, let $\sim_T$ be the equivalence relation on $U(T)$ generated by the pairs $(s(\xi),t(\xi))$ for $\xi\in R(T)$ ([[def-equivalence-relation]], [[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]). The relations are compatible with restriction, so $T\mapsto U(T)/{\sim_T}$ is a presheaf, the naive quotient presheaf $P_{U/R}$. The fppf quotient sheaf $U/R$ is its sheafification ([[def-fppf-sheaf-and-sheafification]], [[lem-fppf-sheafification-exists]]): the initial fppf sheaf receiving $P_{U/R}$. Its construction uses the Axiom of Choice. If $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a field and $G$ is a group scheme of finite type over $k$ ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]]) acting on a $k$-scheme $U$, one takes $R=G\times_kU$ with $s$ the second projection and $t$ the action morphism and writes $U/G$; for $U=G$ and a closed subgroup scheme $H\subseteq G$ ([[def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme]]) acting by right translation one takes $R=G\times_kH$, $s(g,h)=g$, $t(g,h)=gh$, and writes $G/H$. The naive quotient and the quotient sheaf differ in general and no representability is asserted.
items.strategy: Definition fixing the general-base convention. Over a field it agrees with the field-level [[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]] used by the algebraic-group-actions pair. Sheafification exists by [[lem-fppf-sheafification-exists]] under AC, with the universal property of [[def-fppf-sheaf-and-sheafification]]. The distinction between the naive quotient, the fppf quotient sheaf and a representing scheme is exactly the one recorded at field level in that pair; here only the sheaf property is used. Neither flatness nor surjectivity of $s,t$ is assumed in the definition.

items.title: Algebraic spaces over a scheme, defined as fppf sheaves
items.statement: An algebraic space over $S$ is a presheaf of sets $F$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ ([[def-fppf-sheaf-and-sheafification]]) such that: (1) $F$ is an fppf sheaf; (2) the diagonal morphism $F\to F\times F$ is representable by schemes ([[def-representable-morphism-of-presheaves]]); (3) there exists an $S$-scheme $U$ and a morphism $h_U\to F$ which is representable, etale and surjective ([[def-etale-morphism-schemes]], [[def-presheaf-representable-functor-and-representation]], [[def-scheme]]). A morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ is a natural transformation of the underlying presheaves; algebraic spaces over $S$ form a full subcategory of the presheaves of sets on the fppf site. A scheme $X$ over $S$ gives an algebraic space $h_X$, and this is a full embedding. No separatedness, quasi-compactness, finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is part of the definition.
items.strategy: Definition 65.6.1 of Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces* (tag 025Y), exactly at the sheaf level: the diagonal condition makes morphisms from schemes and between algebraic spaces representable, and condition (3) supplies an etale scheme cover. The basic example that every scheme is an algebraic space is Stacks Lemma 65.6.2 (tag 025Z), recorded locally as [[lem-scheme-functor-is-algebraic-space]]. The definition deliberately does not identify $F$ with a quotient sheaf; that identification is a theorem proved later on this page, and the analogous statement fails for stacks (the counterexample on the companion page). The conventions of the site are those of [[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]].

items.title: The standard polynomial resolution has an augmentation contraction and is admissible
items.statement: Let A->B be a map of commutative unital rings and $P_n=(A[-]\,U)^{n+1}(B)$ its standard polynomial simplicial resolution ([[def-standard-resolution-of-a-ring-map]]), where U forgets the algebra. Its augmentation P->B is termwise surjective, a homotopy equivalence of underlying simplicial sets over the constant set B, and a trivial Kan fibration. Its associated A-module complex is a free resolution of B, so it is an admissible polynomial resolution for computing cotangent complexes.
items.strategy: Proof. The free-forgetful unit sends an underlying element x to its polynomial variable [x], and the counit evaluates variables. On the augmented underlying simplicial set, define the extra degeneracy t:P_n->P_{n+1} by x->[x], including B->P_0. The adjunction triangle and naturality give $d_0t=1$, $d_{i+1}t=td_i$, $s_{i+1}t=ts_i$ and $s_0t=tt$, with their augmented interpretations. These identities can also be checked directly on the nested polynomial expressions defining P. For an order map alpha:[n]->[1] with r initial zeros, use $t^r d_0^r$ (using augmentation if r=n+1). These maps commute with every order map by the four identities, and define a homotopy over B between the constant section b->[...[b]...] and id_P. Augmentation followed by that section is therefore homotopic to identity; the other composite is identity. Every augmentation is surjective since nested variables lift every b. Apply [[lem-simplicial-normalization-prism-and-trivial-fibration-criterion]]: underlying-set homotopy equivalence gives a quasi-isomorphism on associated abelian-group complexes, and termwise surjectivity then gives a trivial Kan fibration. Each P_n is a free A-module on its monomials, so the associated complex, cohomologically reindexed in nonpositive degrees, is the claimed free resolution. The extra degeneracy is a set map, not an algebra-linear chain contraction; the normalization/prism lemma is what justifies the passage to module homology.

items.title: Contractible cosimplicial evaluation computes diagram derived colimits
items.statement: Assume AC. Let C be small, R commutative, and U:Delta->C cosimplicial. Suppose each simplicial set $n\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_C(U_n,V)$, V in C, is contractible ([[def-simplicial-set-homotopy-and-trivial-kan-fibration]]). Then, for every contravariant R-module diagram F, the simplicial module chain complex F(U_bullet) is canonically isomorphic to $L\operatorname{colim}_{C^{op}}F$ in D(R). This is functorial in F. The isomorphism is a canonical derived-category roof from projective resolutions; contraction choices are only used to prove its arrows are quasi-isomorphisms.
items.strategy: Proof. Use the supplied representable-sum projective resolution G_p->F of [[lem-projective-representables-and-derived-colimits-of-module-diagrams]], and form the first-quadrant chain double complex A_{p,q}=G_p(U_q), signed on one differential so the total differential squares to zero. For each q, evaluation is exact, so G_p(U_q)->F(U_q) is an augmented exact row. For each p, write G_p as a direct sum of R_V. Then G_p(U_bullet) is a direct sum of the free R-module chains on Hom_C(U_bullet,V); every summand augments to R and is contractible on chains by the prism argument of [[lem-simplicial-normalization-prism-and-trivial-fibration-criterion]]. Its degree-zero augmentation is the map to colim R_V=R, so G_p(U_bullet)->colim G_p is an augmented exact column. Both augmentations give a roof $F(U_\bullet)\leftarrow\operatorname{Tot}A\to\operatorname{colim}G_\bullet$. The maps are quasi-isomorphisms by finite-diagonal elimination: in the augmented cone, the component of a cycle at the largest positive column (respectively row) index is a cycle for the other differential; lift it by exactness, subtract its total boundary, and repeat down to zero. Every total degree has finitely many indices, so the process terminates; no convergence assumption is imported. The right-hand complex computes the derived colimit by the preceding lemma. Comparison lifts between projective resolutions preserve the augmentation roof and are unique up to homotopy; the supplied projective-model theorem makes this roof independent of replacement choices. Naturality in F follows from those comparison lifts. Thus the isomorphism is canonical in D(R), even though choices of contractions were used to prove exactness.

items.title: Morphisms, products and fibre products of algebraic spaces
items.statement: Morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ are the natural transformations of their underlying presheaves ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]]); the category of algebraic spaces over $S$ is a full subcategory of the presheaves on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$. For algebraic spaces $F,G,H$ and morphisms $F\to H$, $G\to H$, the fibre product of presheaves $F\times_HG$ is computed by $(F\times_HG)(T)=F(T)\times_{H(T)}G(T)$ ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]], [[def-presheaf-representable-functor-and-representation]]); it is again an algebraic space over $S$ and represents the fibre product in the category of algebraic spaces. In particular products $F\times_SG$ and the diagonal $\Delta\colon F\to F\times_SF$ are algebraic spaces over $S$; the diagonal is representable by schemes, and a morphism of algebraic spaces is separated when its diagonal is a closed immersion, etale when it is representable etale, and so on ([[def-representable-morphism-of-presheaves]]).
items.strategy: Definitions and the existence of fibre products, following Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Definition 65.6.3 (tag 0260), Lemma 65.7.1 (tag 02X0) and Lemmas 65.7.2-65.7.3 (tags 02X1, 02X2). Proof outline: the presheaf fibre product is a sheaf because finite limits of sheaves are computed pointwise and the sheaf condition is an equalizer condition; its diagonal is the fibre product of the diagonals and is representable because representability is stable under fibre products; an etale surjective cover of the product comes from covers of the two factors, using that etale surjective representable morphisms are stable under products (Stacks 65.5.7, tag 02WM). Only formal properties of representable morphisms are used.

items.title: Every representable functor is an algebraic space
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the quotient/sheaf and descent suppliers. For every $S$-scheme $T$ the representable presheaf $h_T$ ([[def-presheaf-representable-functor-and-representation]]) is an algebraic space over $S$ ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]]): $h_T$ is an fppf sheaf, its diagonal $h_T\to h_T\times h_T=h_{T\times_ST}$ is representable by schemes because $T\times_ST$ is a scheme ([[thm-fibre-products-of-schemes-exist]]), and the identity $h_T\to h_T$ is representable, etale and surjective. Consequently $T\mapsto h_T$ embeds the category of $S$-schemes fully faithfully into the category of algebraic spaces over $S$.
items.strategy: Proof of Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Lemma 65.6.2 (tag 025Z), read in full. The sheaf property is the published [[lem-nonaffine-fppf-descent-of-scheme-morphisms]]; representability of the diagonal reduces to the scheme $T\times_ST$ and the identification $h_T\times h_T=h_{T\times_ST}$; the identity is etale and surjective. Full faithfulness is Yoneda. AC is inherited from the published descent lemma.

items.title: Flat locally finitely presented restrictions give open subquotients
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the quotient-sheaf suppliers. Let $s,t:R\to U$ be an equivalence relation over $S$ with $s,t$ surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, and let $g:U'\to U$ be flat and locally of finite presentation. Form $R'=R\times_{U\times_SU}(U'\times_SU')$ ([[lem-etale-equivalence-relation-restriction]]). Then $U'/R'\to U/R$ is representable by schemes and an open immersion. Its image is the open subquotient corresponding to the saturated open $W=t(s^{-1}(g(U')))\subseteq U$. It is an isomorphism when $W=U$, in particular when $g$ is surjective. No isomorphism or surjectivity is asserted for arbitrary $g$. Here quotient sheaves are those of [[def-quotient-fppf-sheaf-of-a-pre-relation]], and flat/lfp have the meanings of [[def-flat-morphism-schemes]] and [[def-locally-finite-presentation-morphism]].
items.strategy: Reproduce Stacks02WU exactly. Write $W^1=g(U')$ and $W=t(s^{-1}(W^1))$; these are open by [[thm-flat-finite-presentation-is-open]], and the equivalence relation makes $W$ saturated. The map $F'=U'/R'\to F=U/R$ is injective: representatives from $U'$ with the same $F$-class become related fppf-locally, and the unique relation arrow with those two endpoints lies in $R'$. For $a:T\to F$ choose fppf local representatives $a_j:T_j\to U$. On overlaps the relation arrows identify the opens $a_j^{-1}(W)$, so these descend to a unique open $W_T\subseteq T$: the union of their images is open, and saturation makes its inverse images exactly the prescribed opens. The restricted section over $W_T$ lifts locally to $U'$ using the fppf cover $W_j\times_W s^{-1}(W^1)\times_{W^1}U'\to W_j$ (with $t$ used for the map to $W$). Thus $W_T$ represents $T\times_FF'$. Conversely any local lift to $U'$ has its representative in $W$, hence factors through $W_T$. This proves the representable open immersion. If $W=U$, every $W_T=T$ and the map is an isomorphism; a surjective $g$ ensures this condition. In particular a surjective etale cover preserves the quotient, whereas an affine open inclusion merely supplies an open subquotient, as required by02WW. AC is inherited from sheafification and represented-sheaf suppliers.

items.title: Derived colimit commutes with coefficient change and admissible category change
items.statement: Assume AC. For small C and a commutative ring map R->R', there is a canonical isomorphism $L\operatorname{colim}_{C^{op}}F\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'\cong L\operatorname{colim}_{C^{op}}(F\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R')$ for bounded-above R-module diagram complexes F, where the right-hand scalar extension is computed pointwise. For a degree-zero pointwise-flat diagram it is ordinary pointwise tensor. If u:D->C is a functor and W_bullet is cosimplicial in D such that Hom_D(W_bullet,V) and Hom_C(uW_bullet,U) are contractible for all V,U, then the canonical change-of-category map $L\operatorname{colim}_{D^{op}}u^*F\to L\operatorname{colim}_{C^{op}}F$ is an isomorphism for every degree-zero contravariant R-module diagram F.
items.strategy: Proof. Choose the representable-sum projective replacement G of F from [[lem-projective-representables-and-derived-colimits-of-module-diagrams]]. Each G^n evaluates to free R-modules, G tensor_R R' computes the derived scalar extension objectwise, and its terms are sums of the R'-representables. Thus the right-hand derived colimit is colim(G tensor_R R'), equal to (colim G) tensor_R R' because colimits commute with coefficient tensor. Every term of colim G is free R, since colim R_U=R, so the latter tensor also computes the left-hand derived scalar extension. This proves the canonical isomorphism on the actual common projective model; bounded-above flat tensor invariance ([[lem-bounded-above-flat-tensor-complexes-preserve-quasi-isomorphisms]]) proves independence of the model. If F is pointwise flat, objectwise tensor of its projective resolution is exact, so derived scalar extension agrees with ordinary tensor. For the category part, apply [[lem-contractible-cosimplicial-evaluation-computes-derived-colimit]] first to W in D and then to uW in C. Both derived colimits are computed by the same complex F(uW_bullet). The comparison is the identity on this complex: the canonical comparison is obtained by applying u to chains in the bar description of the preceding projective lemma, and the projective/evaluation augmentation roofs commute with those maps. Equivalently lift a projective resolution of u^*F to the restricted projective resolution of F, apply the two augmentation roofs, and use uniqueness up to homotopy to obtain that identity. This proves the comparison is an isomorphism canonically, not an arbitrary existence of isomorphic objects. All tensors here are ordinary module-diagram derived tensors; no simplicial-ring model structure or Quillen adjunction is assumed.
