items.title: Independence of the cotangent complex from the chosen simplicial resolution
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the published derived-tensor and resolution-comparison suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A\to B$ be a map of commutative unital rings. Let $P_\bullet\to B$ and $Q_\bullet\to B$ be polynomial simplicial $A$-algebra resolutions with augmentations that are trivial Kan fibrations of simplicial sets, in the sense of [[def-simplicial-set-homotopy-and-trivial-kan-fibration]] and Stacks92.5.5; the standard resolution is one such resolution ([[def-standard-resolution-of-a-ring-map]], [[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]). Their complexes $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$ and $\Omega_{Q_\bullet/A}\otimes_{Q_\bullet}B$ have canonical identifications with $L_{B/A}$ in $D(B)$ ([[def-cotangent-complex-of-a-ring-map]], [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], [[def-quasi-isomorphism]]); hence they are canonically isomorphic there. The canonical comparison is in the derived category and need not be a distinguished direct chain map between the two chosen complexes. For any commutative square of ordinary ring maps $A\to B$, $A'\to B'$, $A\to A'$ and $B\to B'$, functoriality gives a canonical comparison $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\to L_{B'/A'}$. If the square induces a quasi-isomorphism $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to B'$, this comparison is an isomorphism in $D(B')$. Equivalently, for the ordinary pushout $B'=B\otimes_AA'$, it suffices that $\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(B,A')=0$ for all $i>0$; in particular flat $A\to A'$ suffices. If one writes $B'=B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$, this ordinary-ring statement applies when that derived tensor product is concentrated in degree zero. There is also the valid same-target special case: for composable maps $A\to A'\to B$ such that the canonical map $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to B$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $L_{B/A}\cong L_{B/A'}$ in $D(B)$, for example for a localization $A'=S^{-1}A$ through which $A\to B$ factors. Cohomology and degree shifts are those of [[def-homology-object-of-a-chain-complex]] and [[def-shift-of-a-chain-complex]]. Derived module tensor and its Tor test use [[def-derived-tensor-product-in-the-bounded-above-setting]] and [[prop-homology-of-the-derived-tensor-product-is-tor]]; AC implies the latter supplier's Dependent Choice assumption.
items.strategy: Full local proof, under the stated AC. 1. Choose a bounded small polynomial-factorization category [[def-polynomial-factorization-category-and-cotangent-diagram]] containing the standard resolution and the specified P,Q. For every object A[E]->B, maps into an admissible resolution are precisely the product, over e in E, of its augmentation fibers over the images of e. These fibers and their arbitrary products are contractible by [[lem-trivial-simplicial-fibration-fibres-products-and-contraction]]. Hence the hypotheses of [[lem-contractible-cosimplicial-evaluation-computes-derived-colimit]] hold for each of the three resolutions. Apply that lemma to the cotangent diagram F(P->B)=Omega_P/A tensor_P B. Evaluation on the standard resolution is the definition of L_B/A, and evaluation on P or Q is their stated complex. The three canonical augmentation roofs into the same diagram derived colimit give the required canonical isomorphisms in D(B). The standard resolution is genuinely admissible by [[lem-standard-polynomial-resolution-admissibility]], whose underlying contraction is passed to module homology by [[lem-simplicial-normalization-prism-and-trivial-fibration-criterion]]. Enlargement of the bound is harmless by the category-change lemma with the shared standard resolution. 2. For a commutative ordinary ring square, use the functor u:P->P tensor_A A' between the bounded factorization categories. Standard-resolution functoriality sends a nested variable [p] to the nested variable of its image, giving the canonical map of standard simplicial algebras and hence the canonical cotangent comparison. By [[lem-derived-colimit-coefficient-and-category-change]], coefficient extension changes Lcolim_B F into Lcolim_B'(F tensor_B^L B'). Every value of F is a free B-module, since polynomial differentials are free, so this coefficient tensor is ordinary. Differential base change identifies it with u^*F_{B'/A'} ([[lem-differentials-base-change]]). 3. Assume the canonical derived tensor B tensor_A^L A'->B' is a quasi-isomorphism. The associated A-module complex of the standard resolution is bounded above and free by the admissibility lemma, so its tensor with A' computes this derived tensor using the exact published bounded-above projective/tensor suppliers. Therefore P_bullet tensor_A A'->B' is a quasi-isomorphism. It is termwise surjective: its augmentation in degree zero surjects onto B tensor_A A', whose canonical map to B' is an isomorphism on H0, and degeneracies give the higher surjections. The normalized abelian lifting criterion makes it a trivial Kan fibration. Consequently both the source standard resolution and its image under u satisfy the contractible-cosimplicial hypothesis. The category-change half of the preceding lemma identifies Lcolim_old u^*F_new with Lcolim_new F_new. Composing these coefficient and category comparisons is exactly the canonical cotangent map, so it is an isomorphism. 4. In an ordinary pushout, the derived tensor map is a quasi-isomorphism precisely when higher Tor vanishes, by the published Tor identification under AC implying DC. Flat A->A' implies that vanishing. For A->A'->B and the same-target canonical quasi-isomorphism, take B'=B and the identity on B in the preceding square; this gives the retained localization comparison L_B/A=L_B/A'. Every required ordinary-ring prerequisite is now a supplied local helper or exact published module/differential supplier. This proof makes no claim that the genuine derived-ring/Quillen/module-descent foundations for the separate derived-scheme item are supplied. An augmentation to constant B which is a weak equivalence in the stated simplicial-ring sense is automatically termwise surjective: H0 is B, so P0->B is surjective, and degeneracies give the remaining surjections. The normalized lifting criterion therefore makes the resolution convention in the cotangent definition admissible for this comparison.

items.title: Surjective etale maps from schemes give presentations
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the quotient/sheaf and descent suppliers. Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$ ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]]), let $U$ be an $S$-scheme and let $f\colon U\to F$ be representable, etale and surjective ([[def-representable-morphism-of-presheaves]], [[def-etale-morphism-schemes]]). Set $R=U\times_FU$ ([[def-morphism-and-fibre-products-of-algebraic-spaces]]) and let $j=(t,s)\colon R\to U\times_SU$ be induced by the two projections. Then: (1) $j$ is an equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$ ([[def-groupoid-in-schemes-and-etale-equivalence-relation]]); (2) the projections $s,t\colon R\to U$ are etale; (3) the diagram $R\rightrightarrows U\xrightarrow{f}F$ is a coequalizer in fppf sheaves, that is, $F\cong U/R$ as fppf quotient sheaves ([[def-quotient-fppf-sheaf-of-a-pre-relation]]).
items.strategy: Transcription of Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Lemma 65.9.1 (tag 0262). Steps: (1) $j$ is the base change of the diagonal $F\to F\times F$ along the representable morphism $U\times_SU\to F\times F$, hence a monomorphism, and the groupoid axioms are those of the kernel pair of $f$; (2) etale morphisms are stable under base change, so $s,t$ are etale (published [[lem-etale-stable-base-change-composition]]); (3) the coequalizer statement is checked on fppf sheaves: a section of $F$ over $T$ lifts fppf-locally to $U$ by surjectivity of $f$, and two local lifts agree exactly when their difference lies in $R=U\times_FU$. No finiteness or separation hypotheses are used.

items.title: Gluing algebraic spaces along open subfunctors
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the quotient/sheaf and descent suppliers. Let $F$ be a presheaf of sets on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ ([[def-fppf-sheaf-and-sheafification]]). (1) If $\{F_i\}_{i\in I}$ are algebraic spaces over $S$ ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]]) and the disjoint union of suitable etale scheme covers is representable by an $S$-scheme, then $\coprod_iF_i$ is an algebraic space. (2) Assume $F$ is an fppf sheaf and there are subfunctors $F_i\subseteq F$ such that each $F_i$ is an algebraic space, each inclusion $F_i\to F$ is representable and an open immersion ([[def-representable-morphism-of-presheaves]], [[def-open-immersion-schemes]]), the induced map $\coprod_iF_i\to F$ is surjective as a morphism of sheaves, and $\coprod_iF_i$ is an algebraic space. Then $F$ is an algebraic space over $S$.
items.strategy: Proofs of Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Lemma 65.8.4 (tag 02WQ) and Lemma 65.8.5 (tag 02WR), read in full. (1) The sheaf condition, representability of the diagonal and an etale cover are checked componentwise; the size hypothesis makes the disjoint union of the chosen covers an object of the site. (2) For $T\to F$ the fibre products $F_i\times_FT$ are open subschemes $V_i\subseteq T$; surjectivity of $\coprod F_i\to F$ makes the $V_i$ cover $T$ fppf-locally, and the diagonal of $F$ is obtained by gluing the representable diagonals of the $F_i$ along the open overlaps. Only the sheaf condition and the existence of fibre products of algebraic spaces ([[def-morphism-and-fibre-products-of-algebraic-spaces]]) are used; AC enters only through covers already present in the data.

items.title: Morphisms representable by algebraic spaces
items.statement: Let $F\to G$ be a morphism of presheaves of sets on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ ([[def-fppf-sheaf-and-sheafification]]). It is representable by algebraic spaces when for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $T\to G$ the fibre product $F\times_GT$ is an algebraic space over $S$ ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]], [[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]). This generalizes representability by schemes ([[def-representable-morphism-of-presheaves]]), and a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces stable under base change is attributed to such a morphism fibrewise. A 1-morphism of stacks in groupoids $f\colon\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ over $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ ([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]) is representable by algebraic spaces when for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every 1-morphism $T\to\mathcal Y$ (equivalently, every object $x\in\mathcal Y_T$, by the 2-Yoneda lemma) the 2-fibre product $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y,T}$ is equivalent to the stack in setoids $\mathcal S_Z$ of an algebraic space $Z$ over $T$ ([[def-morphism-and-fibre-products-of-algebraic-spaces]]). Smooth, etale, surjective and other fibrewise properties are then defined by base change.
items.strategy: Definition of Stacks, *Morphisms of Spaces* chapter, Definition 80.3.1 (tag 02YQ), for presheaves, and Stacks, *Properties of Algebraic Stacks*, Definition 101.3.1 and Lemma 101.3.1 (tag 04XR, 04YQ context), for stacks; Vistoli Sections 3.6 and 4.1.1 for representable fibred categories. The 2-Yoneda identification of 1-morphisms $T\to\mathcal Y$ with objects of $\mathcal Y_T$ is Vistoli Section 3.6.2 / Stacks Categories Lemma 4.41; 2-fibre products of stacks in groupoids are stacks in groupoids (Stacks Lemma 8.4.7). The definition contains no smoothness or surjectivity.

items.title: The cotangent complex computes differentials in degree zero and for polynomial algebras
items.statement: Assume AC for the resolution-comparison supplier ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). (1) For every homomorphism $A\to B$ of commutative unital rings one has $H^0(L_{B/A})\cong\Omega_{B/A}$ ([[def-cotangent-complex-of-a-ring-map]], [[def-kahler-differentials-algebra]], [[thm-kahler-differentials-existence-presentation]], [[def-homology-object-of-a-chain-complex]]). (2) If $B$ is a polynomial $A$-algebra, then $L_{B/A}$ is quasi-isomorphic to $\Omega_{B/A}$ placed in degree $0$ ([[def-quasi-isomorphism]]).
items.strategy: Full proof. Write P0=A[B], with symbols [b], and P1=A[P0]. The cokernel of the two face maps on differentials is the free B-module on d[b] modulo d(p)-d[epsilon(p)] for every polynomial p in P0: the two faces send the outer variable [p] to p and to [epsilon(p)]. Taking p=a, [b]+[c] and [b][c] forces d[a]=0, additivity and the Leibniz relation. Conversely those derivation relations imply d(p)=d[epsilon(p)] for every polynomial p, by induction on sums/products. Thus this cokernel represents A-derivations of B, hence is Omega_B/A by the published differential presentation; it is H0 of the standard simplicial differential complex. For polynomial B, the constant simplicial A-algebra B with identity augmentation is a polynomial resolution and identity is a trivial Kan fibration. Apply [[lem-cotangent-complex-resolution-independence]] to compare it canonically with the standard resolution. Its associated differential complex is the constant simplicial module Omega_B/A: the alternating differential is identity in positive even chain degrees and zero in odd degrees. Pair consecutive positive degrees to contract them, leaving Omega_B/A in degree zero. This proves the polynomial clause, without importing an unspecified acyclicity theorem. The full sources are Stacks92.4.5-92.4.7 (08QF-08QH); AC enters only through the newly supplied comparison route.

items.title: Derived schemes and the cotangent complex of a morphism
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the cotangent-comparison suppliers used in the cotangent portion ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). A derived scheme is a pair $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ consisting of a topological space X and a sheaf of simplicial commutative rings $\mathcal O_X$ such that $(X,\pi_0\mathcal O_X)$ is a scheme and each $\pi_i\mathcal O_X$, $i>0$, is a quasi-coherent module on that scheme ([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]], [[def-scheme]], [[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]). Morphisms are taken in the homotopical category of derived locally ringed spaces and induce local morphisms on truncations. A scheme embeds as the constant/discrete derived scheme via $i:\mathit{Sch}\to\mathit{dSch}$. The truncation $t_0(X)=(X,\pi_0\mathcal O_X)$ is right adjoint to this fully faithful inclusion: $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathit{dSch}}(iY,X)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathit{Sch}}(Y,t_0X)$, with the right side discrete. The counit is the canonical morphism $j_X:i(t_0X)\to X$. For a morphism of derived schemes $f:X\to Y$, the cotangent complex $L_{X/Y}$ is a quasi-coherent derived $\mathcal O_X$-module, obtained by gluing the affine derived cotangent complexes: on $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ for derived rings it is the B-module cotangent complex representing relative derived derivations. For discrete ordinary A and B this is the ordinary ring-map complex of [[def-cotangent-complex-of-a-ring-map]], whose resolution/base-change comparisons are commissioned in [[lem-cotangent-complex-resolution-independence]]. The derived pullback $j_X^*L_{X/Y}$ is a complex of $\pi_0\mathcal O_X$-modules on $t_0X$; it must be distinguished from the full derived $\mathcal O_X$-module $L_{X/Y}$. Its homology and shifts use [[def-homology-object-of-a-chain-complex]] and [[def-shift-of-a-chain-complex]]. These constructions require genuine homotopical module and cotangent comparisons, not merely applying the ordinary-ring definition to non-discrete simplicial rings.
items.strategy: Definition and corrected interface, with the full cotangent portion still ESCALATED. Independently read Toën Definition2.1, printed172 (PDF20), Definition2.5 and truncation discussion, printed185 (PDF33), and the quasi-coherent/cotangent module discussion, printed190-192 (PDF38-40). On derived rings the discrete inclusion has left adjoint $\pi_0$; affine spectrum reverses arrows, so on schemes the inclusion is the left adjoint and t0 is the right adjoint. The sheafwise canonical map $\mathcal O_X\to\pi_0\mathcal O_X$ supplies $j_X:t_0X\to X$. Maps from a derived ring to a discrete ring factor through its $\pi_0$, giving the affine mapping equivalence; the local-ring condition and descent glue it over scheme charts. Toën's printed adjunction display should be read with this variance and its explicitly stated canonical map j. The full cotangent complex belongs to the quasi-coherent derived module category over X, not the module category of its truncation; pullback along j gives the separate complex on t0X. Ordinary discrete rings recover Stacks92.3.2, and the now locally proved ordinary comparison item supplies the intended ordinary Tor-independent base-change interface. The general derived cotangent construction requires homotopical modules, universal derived derivations, comparison of valid resolution models and localization/descent of their module complexes. These proofs and suppliers remain unprovided locally, and Toën's survey imports them rather than proves them. The ordinary comparison is now locally closed; the genuinely derived extension/gluing must close before authoring this entire commissioned item; neither portion is deleted or silently replaced by the truncation alone. Ordinary ring comparison is now discharged by the finite local helper packet and [[lem-cotangent-complex-resolution-independence]]. Its product-of-fibers evaluation argument uses only ordinary polynomial factorization and module-diagram homology. That does not supply the genuinely derived simplicial algebra/module Quillen context, derived mapping spaces, affine universal derived derivations or homotopical quasi-coherent descent. The exact HAGII1.2.1.2/1.3.7.2 prerequisites in the blocker map remain the reason this full derived item is escalated. No part of its commissioned statement is deleted.

items.title: Presentations of algebraic spaces
items.statement: A presentation of an algebraic space $F$ over $S$ ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]]) is a pair consisting of an $S$-scheme $U$, an etale equivalence relation $j=(s,t)\colon R\to U\times_SU$ on $U$ over $S$ ([[def-groupoid-in-schemes-and-etale-equivalence-relation]]) and a surjective etale morphism $U\to F$ such that $R=U\times_FU$, i.e. such that $j$ identifies $R$ with the kernel pair of $U\to F$. By [[lem-presentation-from-surjective-etale-map]] every surjective etale morphism from a scheme to $F$ yields a presentation. A presentation is quasi-compact when $U$ is quasi-compact; it is separated, locally separated or locally quasi-finite when $j$ is respectively a closed immersion, an immersion or separated and locally quasi-finite, and these properties depend only on $F$ and not on the chosen presentation.
items.strategy: Definition following Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Definition 65.9.3 (tag 0263). Existence for any surjective etale map from a scheme is [[lem-presentation-from-surjective-etale-map]]. The independence of the presentation for the listed conditions is Stacks Lemma 65.13.1 (tag 02X4) and Lemma 65.11.3; it is stated as a convention and is not used by the structure theorem of this page. The morphism $U\to F$ is representable etale surjective by construction and $R$ is a scheme because the diagonal of $F$ is representable.

items.title: Algebraic stacks and their inertia stacks
items.statement: An algebraic stack (Artin stack) over $S$ is a stack in groupoids $\mathcal X$ over $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ ([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]) such that (1) the diagonal 1-morphism $\Delta\colon\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ is representable by algebraic spaces ([[def-morphism-representable-by-algebraic-spaces]]) and (2) there exist an $S$-scheme $U$ and a 1-morphism $\mathcal S_U\to\mathcal X$ which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective and smooth ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]). Such a pair $(U,\mathcal S_U\to\mathcal X)$ is called a presentation of $\mathcal X$; the stack is Deligne-Mumford when a presentation with $\mathcal S_U\to\mathcal X$ etale can be chosen ([[def-etale-morphism-schemes]]). The inertia stack $\mathcal I_{\mathcal X}$ is the category fibred in groupoids whose fibre category over $T$ has objects the pairs $(x,\alpha)$ with $x\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal X_T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal X_T}(x)$, and morphisms $(x,\alpha)\to(y,\beta)$ over $f\colon T'\to T$ given by morphisms $\gamma\colon f^*x\to f^*y$ with $\gamma\alpha=\beta\gamma$; the projection $\mathcal I_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X$, $(x,\alpha)\mapsto x$, is a 1-morphism. For a 1-morphism $\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ the relative inertia $\mathcal I_{\mathcal X/\mathcal Y}$ imposes the additional condition that the automorphism map to the identity of the image; both are stacks in groupoids when $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ are ([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]).
items.strategy: Definition of Stacks, *Algebraic Stacks*, Definition 94.12.1 (section tag 026N), with the inertia stack from Stacks, *Stacks*, Section 8.7 (tags 036X, 036Y) and *Categories*, Section 4.34 (tag 04Z2). The explicit object-and-morphism description of the inertia is equivalent to the 2-fibre product $\mathcal X\times_{\Delta,\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X,\Delta}\mathcal X$ (Stacks Categories Lemma 4.34.1, tag 034H); the inertia of a stack in groupoids is again a stack in groupoids (Stacks Lemma 8.7.1, tag 036Y). No separatedness or finiteness is assumed. Condition (2) is stated with a 1-morphism from the stack of a scheme; by the conventions of Stacks 94.10.11 this is equivalent to asking for the corresponding representable morphism to be smooth and surjective.

items.title: Quotient maps of etale equivalence relations are etale surjective
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the quotient-sheaf suppliers. Let $j=(s,t)\colon R\to U\times_SU$ be an etale equivalence relation on an $S$-scheme $U$ over $S$ ([[def-groupoid-in-schemes-and-etale-equivalence-relation]]) and let $F=U/R$ be its fppf quotient sheaf ([[def-quotient-fppf-sheaf-of-a-pre-relation]]). If $F$ is an algebraic space over $S$ ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]]), then the canonical morphism $c\colon U\to F$ is representable, etale and surjective; hence $(U,R,U\to F)$ is a presentation of $F$ ([[def-presentation-of-an-algebraic-space]]).
items.strategy: Exact Stacks02WV proof. Since $F$ is already an algebraic space, $U\to F$ is representable: for a scheme $T\to F$, the fiber $T\times_FU$ is the base change of the representable diagonal of $F$ along $(a,c):T\times_SU\to F\times F$. The quotient-sheaf definition supplies fppf local representatives $a_i:T_i\to U$, and the equivalence-relation kernel pair is $U\times_FU\cong R$: equality in the quotient is fppf-local relatedness and unique arrows glue because $R$ is representable and $j$ is a monomorphism. Thus the fiber over $T_i$ is $T_i\times_{a_i,U,t}R$, etale and surjective since $t$ is etale and has the identity section. Etaleness and surjectivity descend on the target fppf cover (affine-local finite presentation, flatness and zero differentials). No separatedness of $t$ is assumed or required here, and no separated locally quasi-finite effectivity theorem is invoked for this already representable fiber. Hence $U\to F$ is etale surjective, with kernel pair $R$, giving the presentation.

items.title: The inertia of a stack in setoids is trivial
items.statement: Let $\mathcal X$ be a stack in groupoids over $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ ([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]) all of whose fibre categories are setoids, i.e. all automorphism groups are trivial. Then the projection $\mathcal I_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X$ from the inertia stack ([[def-algebraic-stack-and-inertia]]) is an equivalence of stacks in groupoids ([[def-category-fibred-in-groupoids]]); conversely, if this projection is an equivalence then every fibre category of $\mathcal X$ is a setoid. In particular, for an algebraic space $Z$ over $S$ ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]]), the fibre category of $\mathcal I_{\mathcal S_Z}$ over $T$ is the discrete groupoid on $\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,Z)$, so $\mathcal I_{\mathcal S_Z}\cong\mathcal S_Z$.
items.strategy: Elementary verification, following Stacks, *Stacks*, Lemma 8.7.1 (tag 036Y) and the comparison statement that algebraic spaces are exactly the algebraic stacks with trivial inertia (Stacks Lemma 101.5.1(3), tag 04SZ). A 1-morphism of stacks in groupoids is an equivalence iff it is fully faithful and essentially surjective on fibre categories; on fibre categories over $T$ the projection sends $(x,\alpha)$ to $x$, with fibre over $x$ the set $\operatorname{Aut}(x)$, and its morphism part is an isomorphism precisely when the automorphism part is determined by $\gamma$. Hence the projection is an equivalence iff all automorphism groups are trivial. For a stack in setoids the only automorphism of each object is its identity; every morphism automatically commutes with these identities. Thus the projection is fully faithful and essentially surjective, hence an equivalence. A setoid may have distinct isomorphic objects and need not be literally discrete. For the particular stack attached to a sheaf, its fibers are discrete by construction, so the asserted discrete-groupoid identification is literal.

items.title: The quotient of an affine etale equivalence relation is an algebraic space
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the quotient and descent suppliers. Let $S$ be a scheme, let $U$ be an affine $S$-scheme and let $j=(s,t)\colon R\to U\times_SU$ be an etale equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$ ([[def-groupoid-in-schemes-and-etale-equivalence-relation]]). Then the fppf quotient sheaf $F=U/R$ ([[def-quotient-fppf-sheaf-of-a-pre-relation]]) is an algebraic space over $S$ ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]]) and $U\to F$ is representable, etale and surjective.
items.strategy: Proof of Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Lemma 65.10.4 (tag 0265), read in full. Step 1: $j$ is a monomorphism, hence separated; $U$ affine makes $U\times_SU$ separated and $R$ separated; $s,t$ are separated etale, the composition $R\to U\times_SU\to U$ is locally of finite type, so $j$ is locally of finite type and, being a monomorphism, locally quasi-finite. Step 2: representability of $c\colon U\to F$: for $T\to F$ choose an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ and $a_i\colon T_i\to U$ as in the proofs of [[lem-quotient-sheaf-base-change-along-flat-lfp-map]] and [[lem-quotient-map-etale-when-quotient-is-algebraic-space]]; then $T_i\times_T(T\times_FU)\cong T_i\times_{a_i,U,t}R$, separated and locally quasi-finite over $T_i$, and the descent datum is effective by [[lem-effective-fppf-descent-separated-locally-quasi-finite]]. Step 3: etaleness and surjectivity of $U\to F$ follow since its base changes are base changes of the etale surjective $t$. Step 4: representability of the diagonal $F\to F\times F$: the square with $R\to U\times_SU$ and the diagonal is cartesian, $U\times_SU\to F\times F$ is representable etale surjective, and representability is fppf-local on the target, again by effectivity of descent for separated locally quasi-finite morphisms (the pullbacks of $j$ are separated and locally quasi-finite; $j$ itself need not be etale). The affine hypothesis is used only in Step 1 to obtain separatedness of $U\times_SU$ and $R$. The open-subquotient lemma is used only for local representatives; no nonsurjective restriction is treated as preserving the whole quotient. AC is inherited from the exact descent suppliers.

items.title: Quotients of schemes by etale equivalence relations are algebraic spaces
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the quotient and descent suppliers. Let $S$ be a scheme, let $U$ be an $S$-scheme and let $j=(s,t)\colon R\to U\times_SU$ be an etale equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$ ([[def-groupoid-in-schemes-and-etale-equivalence-relation]]). Then the fppf quotient sheaf $U/R$ ([[def-quotient-fppf-sheaf-of-a-pre-relation]]) is an algebraic space over $S$ ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]]), and $U\to U/R$ is representable, etale and surjective; consequently $(U,R,U\to U/R)$ is a presentation of $U/R$ ([[def-presentation-of-an-algebraic-space]]).
items.strategy: Proof of Stacks, *Algebraic Spaces*, Theorem 65.10.5 (tag 02WW), read in full. Steps: (1) by [[lem-quotient-map-etale-when-quotient-is-algebraic-space]] it suffices to prove that $U/R$ is an algebraic space; (2) replacing $U$ by a surjective etale cover $U'\to U$ does not change the quotient: the restriction $R'=R|_{U'}$ is an etale equivalence relation by [[lem-etale-equivalence-relation-restriction]] and $U/R\cong U'/R'$ by [[lem-quotient-sheaf-base-change-along-flat-lfp-map]]; choosing $U'=\coprod_iU_i$ with $U_i$ affine open reduces to the case where $U$ is a disjoint union of affine schemes; (3) for each $i$ the restriction $R_i$ is an etale equivalence relation, $F_i=U_i/R_i$ is an algebraic space with $U_i\to F_i$ etale surjective by [[lem-affine-etale-equivalence-relation-quotient]], and the induced maps $F_i\to F$ are representable open immersions by the open-subquotient clause, with $\coprod_iF_i\to F$ surjective ([[lem-quotient-sheaf-base-change-along-flat-lfp-map]]); (4) $\coprod_iF_i$ is an algebraic space (part (1) of [[lem-open-immersion-gluing-of-algebraic-spaces]] with the covers $U_i$) and all hypotheses of part (2) hold, so $F$ is an algebraic space; (5) $U\to U/R$ is representable etale surjective by [[lem-quotient-map-etale-when-quotient-is-algebraic-space]], and the presentation statement is the definition. The two uses of02WU are distinct: the first is a surjective etale covering and hence an isomorphism; each individual affine inclusion uses only the representable open immersion. Their images cover because the affine opens cover the original U. AC is inherited from sheafification and the corrected descent chain.

title: Algebraic Spaces, Stacks, and Derived Algebraic Geometry Foundations — Examples

items.title: The affine line is an algebraic space
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the quotient/sheaf and descent suppliers. Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathbb A^1_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ ([[def-affine-scheme]], [[def-scheme-over-base]]). Then $\mathbb A^1_k$ is an algebraic space over $k$ ([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]]). A presentation is given by $U=\mathbb A^1_k$, the diagonal equivalence relation $R=\Delta(\mathbb A^1_k)\subseteq\mathbb A^1_k\times_k\mathbb A^1_k$ with its two projections ([[def-groupoid-in-schemes-and-etale-equivalence-relation]]), and the identity $U\to\mathbb A^1_k$; more generally every $k$-scheme is an algebraic space ([[lem-scheme-functor-is-algebraic-space]]).
items.strategy: Verification: by [[lem-scheme-functor-is-algebraic-space]] the representable functor $h_{\mathbb A^1}$ is an algebraic space. The diagonal relation $R=\Delta(\mathbb A^1)$ has $s,t$ equal to inverse isomorphisms onto $U$, so it is an etale equivalence relation; its quotient sheaf is $h_{\mathbb A^1}$ because the relation is already the kernel pair of the identity, and the identity is etale and surjective. The example also records that the etale equivalence relation of a presentation need not be finite or separated over $U$.

items.title: The classifying stack of a finite group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the descent suppliers below. Let $k$ be a field and let $G$ be a finite group (for instance $G=\mathbb Z/2$), viewed as the constant group scheme $G_k$ over $k$ ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]]), acting trivially on $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $BG$ be the category fibred in groupoids over $(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ ([[def-category-fibred-in-groupoids]], [[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]]) whose fibre category over a $k$-scheme $T$ has as objects the right $G$-torsors over $T$ - fppf coverings $P\to T$ with a right $G$-action such that $G_k\times_kP\to P\times_TP$, $(g,p)\mapsto(pg,p)$, is an isomorphism - and as morphisms the isomorphisms of torsors. Then $BG$ is a stack in groupoids over $(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ ([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]) and an algebraic stack over $k$ ([[def-algebraic-stack-and-inertia]]) with presentation $\operatorname{Spec}k\to BG$ given by the trivial torsor $G_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. For the trivial torsor $G_T$, the automorphism sheaf as a right $G$-torsor is $G_T$ by left multiplication. If $G$ is abelian, for every torsor $P$ over $T$ its automorphism sheaf is canonically $G_T$ by right translation, and the inertia stack satisfies $\mathcal I_{BG}\cong G_k\times_kBG$; over the trivial torsor in $BG(\operatorname{Spec}k)$ the inertia objects are the pairs (trivial torsor, $g$) with $g\in G$.
items.strategy: Verification over arbitrary test schemes, under the AC of the published descent suppliers. (1) A right torsor $P\to T$ in the statement trivializes over its own fppf cover by the given kernel-pair isomorphism. Over an affine open of $T$, refine this cover by finitely many affine opens of $P$ whose images cover the target; flat lfp morphisms are open. Their disjoint union $V\to T$ is an affine faithfully flat quasi-compact lfp refinement, and $P_V\cong G_V$ is finite etale. Its canonical descent datum is effective by [[thm-effective-fpqc-descent-of-finite-etale-covers]]. The descended finite etale scheme represents the same fppf sheaf as $P$, since their compatible local isomorphisms glue by [[lem-nonaffine-fppf-descent-of-scheme-morphisms]]; Yoneda identifies it with $P$. Thus every such torsor is finite etale and surjective over $T$, without any Noetherian assumption. Pullbacks of torsors therefore exist. (2) For a family of torsors with cocycle-compatible isomorphisms, refine an arbitrary fppf covering over each affine target open by a finite affine covering. Apply the finite-etale descent theorem on the single resulting affine fpqc refinement. The $G$-actions descend as morphisms, and the kernel-pair isomorphism descends with its inverse by the represented-sheaf supplier; the resulting finite etale scheme is a torsor, with surjectivity detected on the cover. Uniqueness and descent of equivariant maps follow from the same suppliers and glue across target opens. Hence $BG$ is a stack in groupoids. (3) For two torsors $P,Q$ over any $T$, their common finite etale surjective cover $U=P\times_TQ\to T$ trivializes both. The equivariant Isom sheaf becomes $G_U$, with transition maps induced by the two torsor trivializations; these satisfy the cocycle identity. Effective finite-etale descent represents it by a finite etale $T$-scheme. This proves representability of the diagonal $BG\to BG\times BG$, because its base change along the pair $(P,Q)$ is precisely this Isom sheaf. (4) The trivial torsor defines $\operatorname{Spec}k\to BG$; its base change by the object $P/T$ is the scheme $P$, since an equivariant isomorphism from $G_{T'}$ to $P_{T'}$ is determined by the image of the identity. Step (1) proves that this base change is finite etale and surjective, hence smooth and surjective; etale is standard smooth of relative dimension zero. Thus the morphism is a presentation and $BG$ is algebraic for every finite group $G$. This uses target fpqc descent of finite etale covers, not smoothness being local on the source. (5) On a trivial right torsor, equivariant automorphisms are left multiplication by $G(T)$. For a general torsor the local identifications differ by conjugation; if $G$ is abelian the conjugation transitions are identities. Equivalently right translation by a section of $G_T$ gives a canonical automorphism. Therefore $\operatorname{Aut}_G(P)\cong G_T$ in the abelian case, naturally with respect to torsor isomorphisms, and $\mathcal I_{BG}\cong G_k\times_kBG$. Arbitrary torsors over $k$ need not be trivial; the stated inertia calculation over the trivial torsor is sufficient for the counterexample.

items.title: A quotient stack need not be a scheme
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the quotient-sheaf and classifying-stack suppliers. Let $k$ be a field and let $G$ be a nontrivial finite group, viewed as the constant group scheme over $k$ ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]]); for instance $G=\mathbb Z/2$. The classifying stack $BG$ of [[ex-classifying-stack-of-a-finite-group]] is an algebraic stack over $k$ ([[def-algebraic-stack-and-inertia]]) but is not equivalent to the stack $\mathcal S_X$ of any $k$-scheme $X$ ([[def-scheme]], [[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]). In particular, the quotient stack of the trivial action of $G$ on $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is not a scheme, although the corresponding fppf quotient sheaf ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]) is the representable sheaf $h_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$: the passage from quotient sheaves to quotient stacks genuinely enlarges the category.
items.strategy: Proof under the AC hypotheses of the two suppliers. For a $k$-scheme $X$, the fibre category of $\mathcal S_X$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the discrete groupoid on the set $X(k)=\operatorname{Mor}_k(\operatorname{Spec}k,X)$ ([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]); in particular all its automorphism groups are trivial, and by [[lem-inertia-of-a-stack-in-setoids]] its inertia is itself. An equivalence of stacks in groupoids induces equivalences of fibre categories ([[def-category-fibred-in-groupoids]]), and a groupoid equivalent to a discrete groupoid has trivial automorphism groups. But the fibre category $BG(\operatorname{Spec}k)$ contains the trivial torsor $G_k$, whose automorphism group is $G_k(k)\cong G$ by the automorphism computation of [[ex-classifying-stack-of-a-finite-group]]; this group is nontrivial, a contradiction. Finally, for the trivial action the naive quotient presheaf of the pre-relation $G\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k\rightrightarrows\operatorname{Spec}k$ is already $h_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$, so its fppf quotient sheaf is $h_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]] is the field-level convention used for this comparison); the quotient stack is $BG$, which is not even a scheme. The example separates quotient sheaves, algebraic spaces and stacks.
